blogs.title: FeatLLM Unlocked: How Large Language Models Are Becoming Expert Feature Engineers
blogs.description: An introductory deep‑dive into the FeatLLM framework that repurposes LLMs from end‑to‑end predictors to automatic feature engineers for tabular data. We explain why generating rules instead of per‑sample predictions cuts inference costs dramatically, eliminates the need for fine‑tuning, and overcomes prompt‑size limits that plague earlier methods like TabLLM or STUNT.

blogs.title: Inside the Prompt: Crafting Effective In‑Context Instructions for Rule Extraction
blogs.description: A step‑by‑step walkthrough of FeatLLM’s three‑part prompt design—basic information description, reasoning instruction with a two‑step chain‑of‑thought, and response instruction. Learn how these prompts coax the LLM to first understand causal relationships between features and the task, then derive concise decision rules for each class, all without exposing the model to spurious correlations.

blogs.title: From Text to Tensors: Turning LLM‑Generated Rules into Binary Features
blogs.description: This post explains how natural‑language rules are transformed into machine‑readable binary features. We cover the parsing pipeline that uses the LLM itself to emit clean Python code from noisy rule text, execution of that code via `exec()`, and construction of per‑class binary indicators that feed into a simple downstream model.

blogs.title: Bagging and Ensembling in FeatLLM: Taming Prompt Length Limits While Boosting Robustness
blogs.description: Explore why FeatLLM builds an ensemble of rule sets through bagging and temperature sampling. The article details how random feature/instance subsets keep prompts within token limits on wide tables, how multiple diverse rule collections are combined via probability averaging, and why this strategy dramatically reduces performance degradation from irrelevant or noisy columns.

blogs.title: Performance Showdown: FeatLLM vs Traditional & LLM‑Based Tabular Learners
blogs.description: "FeatLLM" goes head‑to‑head with logistic regression, XGBoost, Random Forests, SCARF, STUNT, TabPFN, In‑Context Learning, TABLET and TabLLM across 13 public datasets. We break down AUC scores, highlight the average ~10 % gain over competing LLM approaches, illustrate how only 4 shots match conventional models trained on 32 shots, and compare training/inference latency.

blogs.title: Deploying FeatLLM with API‑Only Access – A Practical Guide
blogs.description: A hands‑on tutorial for practitioners who only have access to an LLM inference API (e.g., GPT‑3.5). The guide covers issuing a single batch of rule‐generation queries per dataset, persisting generated code locally, training the lightweight linear weight model on binary features without further API calls, setting temperature & ensemble size, estimating cost per run, and best practices for scaling.

blogs.title: Beware the Biases: Ethical Implications of LLM‑Powered Feature Engineering
blogs.description: Because FeatLLM leans heavily on prior knowledge baked into large language models, hidden societal biases or misinformation can surface in automatically generated rules—especially in high‑stakes domains like healthcare or finance. This post discusses potential bias pathways identified in the paper’s broader impact section and proposes mitigation tactics such as rule auditing by domain experts, fairness‐aware prompting, and post‑hoc validation.
